title: Wholesale Sakhar: Bulk Himalayan Jaggery from Sankhuwasabha
seoTitle: Wholesale Jaggery Nepal: Bulk Sakhar from the Hills
description: Bulk wood-fired sakhar for shops, cafes, sweet makers and hamper buyers in Nepal. What we supply, how we quote, and how to order direct from the farm.
content:
Most of the enquiries we get from businesses start the same way: someone has been buying our sakhar (सख्खर), or jaggery, one kilo at a time for their shop or their kitchen, and it has stopped making sense.

This page is for those buyers. It is shorter than the rest of our writing on purpose, because a shop owner comparing suppliers wants facts and a phone number, not a story about a wood fire.

> We supply hill sakhar in bulk from Sankhuwasabha in two forms: the 1 kg block and the sakhar powder. Quantities, price breaks and lead times depend on the form, the volume and where the season is, so we quote rather than publish a rate card. Message +977-9860149199 on WhatsApp with what you need and we will come back with a real number.

## Who Buys Sakhar in Bulk From Us

- **Organic and kirana shops** reselling by the block or repacking into their own smaller units.
- **Cafes and tea houses** sweetening chiya at volume, which is by some distance the most common use.
- **Sweet and mithai makers** using jaggery as a base ingredient.
- **Chaku makers** ahead of Maghe Sankranti, who need a hard, low-moisture block and need it early.
- **Bakeries and restaurants** using it where a caramel note and a darker crumb are wanted.
- **Corporate gift and hamper buyers** around Dashain and Tihar.
- **Hotels** stocking it at breakfast or in guest rooms.

Two of those are seasonal and worth planning around properly. Chaku makers and hamper buyers both order in volume, on a calendar everyone in the country shares, which means the worst possible time to place a large order is the week everybody else does.

## What We Can Supply

We make two things, and we would rather be a good supplier of two products than a mediocre one of ten.

:::table Bulk sakhar forms and what each one suits
Form | Retail pack | What it suits
Sakhar Block | 1 kg, hand-poured discs | Chaku making, cooking, mithai, shops reselling by weight
Sakhar Powder | 250 g sealed pouch | Cafes and tea houses, anywhere it is spooned into a cup
:::

Our published retail prices are Rs. 400 per kg for the [block](/products/organic-jaggery-block) and Rs. 149 for 250 g of [powder](/products/jaggery-powder). Those are the anchor. Bulk pricing sits below them and depends on volume, and we will quote it rather than guess at it here.

The blocks are poured by hand, so individual discs vary and a kilo is made up to weight rather than to a fixed count. If your own packing needs a consistent piece count rather than a consistent weight, tell us before you order, because that changes what we can promise.

## Pricing, Quantities and Lead Times

We are going to be straight about why there is no rate card on this page.

Sakhar is a seasonal product made in batches on a hillside. What we can supply, how quickly, and at what price all move with where the season is and what has already been committed. A price list published in August and read in January would be wrong in both directions, and a supplier who quotes you a stale number is a supplier who will later explain why they cannot honour it.

So: tell us the form, the quantity and the date you need it, and we will give you a real figure and a real lead time for that order.

What we can say in general terms is that the price breaks are by volume, that lead time is longer during the crushing season than outside it, and that anything for mid-January should be agreed months rather than weeks in advance.

## Packaging and Labelling

Retail packing is a kraft pouch with our own sticker on it. For bulk we can talk about other options, including plainer packing for buyers repacking into their own brand.

Whether we can supply unbranded or white-label stock, and in what pack sizes, is a question we would rather answer for your specific order than in the abstract, because it depends on volume. Ask.

## What Chemical-Free Means Here, and What It Does Not

This matters more for a wholesale buyer than a retail one, because you may be making a claim of your own on the back of ours.

What we mean by chemical-free is this. The cane is grown on hill terraces without chemical fertiliser or pesticide. The juice is boiled in an iron kadhai over a wood fire and skimmed by hand. No sulphur, no chemical clarifier, no bleaching agent, no added colour, no anti-caking agent in the powder. That is a description of a method.

It is not the same thing as a certification. If your own labelling, your own buyers or your own compliance require certified organic documentation, ask us before you place an order and we will tell you precisely what paperwork we can and cannot provide. Do not assume, and please do not print a certification claim on your packaging on the strength of a sentence on a supplier's website. That applies to every supplier, not only to us.

The honest technical background is that the composition of unrefined cane sugar varies with cane variety, soil and processing method. That is not a flaw in anyone's production; it is the nature of [non-centrifugal cane sugar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-centrifugal_cane_sugar), and it is documented in the [Sugar Tech review of the category](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8314846/). Which brings us to the next section.

## Batch Variation, and Who Should Not Buy From Us

Hill sakhar varies between batches. Colour shifts with how late in the season the cane was cut and how long that kadhai ran. Hardness and moisture move with it. The taste carries woodsmoke, and how much depends on the fire.

For some buyers that is the whole appeal. For others it is a problem, and we would rather say so here than discover it after you have taken delivery.

You should probably not buy from us if you need a pale, neutral sweetener that behaves identically in every batch, if your product depends on a fixed colour, or if you are buying purely on price. Terai gur is made at a larger scale on flat land, it is cleaner tasting, more consistent and cheaper, and for those requirements it is simply the better material. We have written the full comparison in [what makes hill sakhar different](/blog/himalayan-jaggery-sankhuwasabha).

Turning away an order that was never going to work is cheaper for both of us than a return.

## What We Would Need From You to Quote

1. Which form, block or powder, and roughly what split if both.
2. Quantity, in kilos, and whether it is a one-off or a repeating order.
3. The date you need it in hand, not the date you would like to order.
4. Where it is going, since delivery outside the valley changes the cost and the timing.
5. Whether you need our packing, plainer bulk packing or your own label.
6. Any documentation your business requires.

Six answers is usually enough for us to come back with a firm number.

## How to Order

WhatsApp is fastest: **+977-9860149199**. The same number takes calls.

You can also use the [contact form](/contact), which reaches us either way. For retail quantities, everything is on the [shop](/shop) at the prices linked above, and [what those prices are made of](/blog/sakhar-price-in-nepal) is set out in full.

If you want to see the operation before you commit to a volume, that is [here](/our-story), and we are happy to answer questions before there is any order on the table.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the minimum order for wholesale sakhar?

It depends on the form and the time of year, so we set it per enquiry rather than publishing a single figure. Message us with the quantity you have in mind and we will tell you straight away whether it is workable.

### Do you offer bulk discounts?

Yes. Bulk pricing sits below our published retail prices of Rs. 400 per kg for the block and Rs. 149 for 250 g of powder, with breaks by volume. We quote against a specific order rather than publishing a rate card, because sakhar is seasonal and a stale price list helps nobody.

### Can you supply unbranded sakhar for our own label?

Possibly, depending on volume and pack size. It is a real question with a real answer, but the answer changes with the order, so ask us with your quantity and packing requirement and we will tell you what is feasible.

### How long does a bulk order take?

Lead time depends on the season and on what is already committed. Orders for mid-January, when chaku and festival demand peak, should be agreed months in advance rather than weeks. Outside that window we can usually move faster.

### Do you deliver outside Kathmandu?

Yes, we ship pan-Nepal. Cost and timing depend on the destination and the weight, and hill and remote deliveries take longer, particularly during monsoon. Terms are on our [shipping page](/shipping-policy).

### Is your sakhar certified organic?

We grow without chemical fertiliser or pesticide and make without additives, which is what we mean by chemical-free. Whether we hold certification that satisfies your particular compliance requirement is a question to ask us directly before ordering, and we will answer it precisely rather than in marketing language.

## In Short

Two products, made in small batches on hill terraces in Sankhuwasabha, sold in bulk to buyers who want what a wood fire does to cane juice and can live with a block that is not identical every time.

If that is you, message +977-9860149199 with the six answers above and you will get a real quote rather than a brochure.

If it is not you, we would genuinely rather tell you now.
author: Rashmita Bhandari
authorBio: Rashmita founded SakharSansar in 2024 and runs it end to end — she tends the wood fire, pours the moulds and packs every block by hand. The cane comes off the terraces her family and forty-one neighbouring households farm in Sankhuwasabha, the way they have made sakhar for seven generations.
